local.help:
Manage Rigbox workspaces, apps, and tools

Usage: rigbox [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  ai            Configure account-level AI defaults and view usage
  api           Send a raw authenticated request to the Rigbox API
  api-key       Manage account API keys
  ci            Manage GitHub Actions deployment bindings
  capacity      Show fleet workspace-slot capacity
  config        View or set persisted CLI defaults (output, pager)
  completions   Generate or install a shell completion script
  limits        Show effective resource limits and current usage
  login         Authenticate with Rigbox
  logout        Remove saved credentials
  service-spec  Manage account-level service specs
  setup-script  Manage reusable workspace setup scripts
  ssh           Manage SSH public keys for your account
  status        Show dashboard summary for the current account
  uninstall     Remove the local Rigbox CLI install
  update        Update the Rigbox CLI to the latest published release
  whoami        Show the current user and workspace
  app           Manage apps inside a workspace
  init          Scaffold a rig.yaml for the current directory
  snapshot      Manage workspace snapshots
  volume        Manage persistent volumes
  build         Build reproducible images and view build logs
  release       Manage workspace releases
  app-release   List and roll back apps without replacing the workspace
  rollback      Reverse a preview promotion, or activate a specific release
  tools         Launch and manage workspace tools
  deploy        Deploy the project from its rig.yaml
  publish       Publish the project to the community registry
  workspace     Manage workspace lifecycle and configuration
  recipe        Publish and install community recipes
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: human, or `rig config set output …`]
          
          [possible values: human, json, yaml, text, table]

      --query <JMESPATH>
          Filter output with a JMESPath expression

      --cli-input-json <FILE>
          Read inputs from a JSON file or '-' (stdin)

      --cli-input-yaml <FILE>
          Read inputs from a YAML file or '-' (stdin)

      --generate-cli-skeleton
          Print a fillable input template, then exit

      --no-pager
          Do not pipe help output through a pager

  -v, --verbose
          Verbose diagnostics on stderr: per-phase deploy tracing, job-poll status, and transport commands. Useful for debugging a slow or stuck `rig deploy`

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version

Stage a change before swinging production traffic at it; pair with `--promote` to swap atomically (zero-downtime). `<suffix>` stages an sibling app at `<base>-<suffix>` on its own subdomain. The special value `preview` instead clones the WHOLE workspace into a hidden preview (every app), overlays your new code, and serves it at `<app>-pv-<id>.rigbox.dev` — `--promote` then re-homes prod onto it.

Pick by what the workspace IS: `preview` is for production SERVICE hosts (it swaps to a new workspace, so the old one is retired — open SSH sessions in it don't follow the swap). For a workspace people actively work IN (SSH, shells, dev processes), deploy in place or use `<suffix>` (same workspace, ~1s app restart) so sessions and workspace state survive.

After staging via `--bluegreen <suffix>`, swap the production subdomain to the staged sibling in one atomic DB transaction (zero-downtime). The previous production app is retained as a rollback target until you delete it.

Requires `--bluegreen`.
